triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '16. K-decay scratch is algebraically removable' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 16. K-decay scratch is algebraically removable

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 16. K-decay scratch is algebraically removable

payload.attempted: Treat the state update as requiring a materialized K-decay scratch tile:
payload.lesson: For recurrences of the form `K^T @ diag(decay) @ V`, choose the side that minimizes scratch. In this shape, scaling `v_new` eliminates K-decay scratch and drops K1 from `706.40 us` to `607.33 us`.

established_fact.mechanism: The decay multiply is separable over `t` and can be moved to the V operand:

payload.observed: Even after R2S, the scratch path consumed millions of shared loads and pack instructions. It kept K1 at `706.40 us` in V29.
payload.root_cause: The decay multiply is separable over `t` and can be moved to the V operand:

implementation.snippet:
```text
state += (K[t,k] * exp_decay[t]) @ v_new[t,v]
```

```text
sum_t (K[t,k] * exp_decay[t]) * v_new[t,v]
==
sum_t K[t,k] * (exp_decay[t] * v_new[t,v])
```
